data.title: Mistral Plans to Double Asia Headcount as It Opens Regional Hub in Singapore
data.description:
(02:14 GMT) *Mistral Establishes Asia-Pacific Headquarters in Singapore to Build Sovereign AI Capabilities
(02:14 GMT) *Mistral: Aim to More Than Double APAC Headcount to 200 by 2027
(02:15 GMT) *Mistral: Hiring in Areas of Science, Engineering, Applied AI, Robotics
(02:42 GMT) Mistral Plans to Double Asia Headcount as It Opens Regional Hub in Singapore

By Kimberley Kao

French artificial-intelligence startup Mistral has established its Asia-Pacific headquarters in Singapore, as it seeks to meet growing demand for sovereign AI capabilities in the region.

Mistral said Friday that it aims to more than double its Asia-Pacific headcount to 200 by 2027, hiring in the areas of science, engineering, applied AI and robotics. This strategic investment will support the ambition to accelerate the development, training and real-world deployment of sovereign AI models, it said.

"Our ambition is to establish Singapore as a strategic location for empowering governments and enterprises across Asia-Pacific to retain ownership of their infrastructure and intelligence, and translate these into lasting economic value and industrial competitiveness," said Arthur Mensch, co-founder and chief executive of Mistral.

The announcement comes shortly after Mistral completed a new funding round in September, led by South Korea's Samsung Electronics, that lifted its valuation above $24 billion, giving it additional firepower to invest in model development and grow its customer base.

Write to Kimberley Kao at kimberley.kao@wsj.com

data.title: Lynas shareholder meeting to spotlight CEO hunt next week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Lynas shareholder meeting in Sydney on November 25
  • Succession process to replace Amanda Lacaze started in January
  • Lynas says highly credentialed candidate withdrew from process

By Melanie Burton

The prolonged hunt for a new CEO to lead Lynas Rare Earths will be front and centre at its annual shareholder meeting next week, after the West's top producer of the strategic metals said a favoured candidate withdrew.

Former CEO Amanda Lacaze announced her retirement in January, and some investors say the extended search to replace her has left the company vulnerable to a takeover, especially after a 42% share-price slide from a 15-year high hit in April.

Lynas is the only commercial producer of both light and heavy rare earths outside China and by far the most advanced in building a supply chain from mine to magnet, key to the West's push to diversify procurement for a wide range of industries, from electric vehicles and robotics to defence.

"Considering the barriers to entry and strategic importance of this sector, corporate appeal is likely to be the highest it's been in some time," said Sam Berridge, a portfolio manager with Perennial Partners in Perth.

Lynas chairman John Humphrey said last month he expected to announce a new CEO before the annual general meeting in Sydney on November 25. The board suspended the search earlier this year while it was in talks on a merger that did not go ahead. The hunt was delayed further after a contender pulled out.

"Lynas Chairman, John Humphrey, has previously confirmed that a highly credentialed candidate withdrew from the process for personal reasons prior to being interviewed by the full Board," said head of investor relations Daniel Havas.

Fund managers said that suggested the search may extend past next week.

"Lynas is a unique company, and the Board wants to ensure the right appointment is made," Havas said by email. "The Board has great confidence in our Interim CEO and the highly experienced senior leadership team to continue to run operations and implement the Towards 2030 growth strategy."

Pol Le Roux, previously chief operating officer, has acted as interim CEO since the end of June.

TOUGH GIG

Finding a replacement for "a superstar CEO" such as Amanda Lacaze, who was at the helm for 12 years, may prove tough, said Matthew Hope, a resources analyst with Ord Minnett.

The company's 2030 growth plan and October deal to buy a rare earths mine in Brazil will make it hard for a new CEO to make their mark, while development plans will be costly, suggesting it may be hard to boost Lynas' share price and earn incentives, he said.

Investors have been unimpressed by how long the search has taken, with some suggesting it has left the company vulnerable to a predator. Major gold producer Newmont seized a chance to buy Australia's biggest gold producer Newcrest Mining when it was without a permanent CEO in 2023.

While Lynas shares have held up better than other critical minerals companies hit by concerns about a slowdown in data centre growth, they are trading on a forward EV/EBITDA multiple broadly in line with 10-year lows, Perennial's Berridge said.

Meanwhile, demand for rare earth metals remains solid, backed by a US push to replace missile inventories, robust demand growth for industrial robots and steady global EV sales, he said.

data.title: India picks Coal India group for rare earth magnet plant
data.description:
Coal India Limited (BSE: 533278) has received a letter of intent from India's Ministry of Heavy Industries to build a plant making sintered rare earth permanent magnets, the company said in a filing with the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India on November 19. The consortium it leads with NFTDC was declared the L2 bidder under the government's Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet.

The award takes the coal producer into the production of neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets, a product outside its core mining business. The ministry is backing domestic manufacturing of these magnets through the scheme. The ministry issued the letter of intent on November 19. Under its terms, the consortium will set up the facility through a special purpose vehicle formed under the scheme.

The plant is to have a capacity of 1,200 tonnes per annum, according to the filing. The contract runs for seven years. That period covers two years of pre-construction work and five years of operation. Coal India classified the order as domestic. The company said its promoter, promoter group and group companies had no interest in the ministry as the awarding entity. It added that the contract would not fall within related party transactions.

data.title: Japan's Nikkei falls more than 4% after Anthropic's IPO fails to restore AI confidence
data.description:
By Junko Fujita

Japan's Nikkei stock average fell more than 4% on Friday to touch a seven-month low, as technology shares tumbled after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore confidence in AI trade.

The Nikkei fell as much as 4.85% to 56,594.94, its lowest level since mid-April, and was down 4.33% to 56,871.78 as of 0210 GMT.

The broader Topix fell 2.89% to 3,711.87.

"There was a high expectation that Anthropic's market debut may lift sentiment for AI-related shares, but that hope faded as its price pared gains," said Hiroyuki Ueno, chief strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management.

Shares of Anthropic , the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, opened 34% higher than the $83 IPO price set on Wednesday. But the stock pared gains and closed at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price.

In Japan, chip-related Advantest and Tokyo Electron slipped 10.15% and 6.07%, respectively. Technology investor SoftBank Group tumbled 14.4% and memory chip maker Kioxia lost 11.62%,

"Investors realise that these chip shares became cheap, but they are afraid to pick them up because they are afraid there may be another dip in the market," said Ueno.

Bucking the trend, insurers rose, with Tokio Marine Holdings rising 3% to become the top percentage gainer on the Nikkei. MS&AD Insurance and Sompo Holdings rose 2.83% and 1.71%, respectively.

Drug makers rose, with Takeda Pharmaceutical and Shionogi & Co gaining 0.63% and 0.4%, respectively.

Of more than 1,500 stocks trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's prime market, 90% fell, 8% rose and 1% traded flat.

data.title: Trek Metals Highlights Christmas Creek Potential with High-Grade Manganese Hits at Kuro
data.description:
Trek Metals has returned manganese grades of up to 40.3% from its final drilling assays at the Kuro discovery within the Christmas Creek project in Western Australia.

The strongest result was 25 metres grading 31.4% manganese from 18m downhole, including a 12m interval grading 40.3%, as Trek completed its first manganese drilling season.

Across two drilling phases, 48 of 122 holes at Kuro delivered significant manganese intersections, including 31 holes with grades exceeding 20%.

The latest work closes the 2026 campaign and gives Trek a new set of geological and geophysical data to assess before selecting targets for next year.

Shallow Grades Define Discovery

Phase two involved 50 reverse circulation holes testing electrical chargeability anomalies around the initial Kuro discovery, with 10 returning significant manganese intersections above 5%.

Six of those holes contained intersections above 20%, while other notable results included 6m grading 24.4% from 9m and 6m grading 21.1% from 7m.

The main 25m intersection also contained an 8m interval grading 29.9%, and its highest individual one-metre assay reached 49.9% manganese.

All significant intersections in the final batch were encountered between 5m and 51m downhole, with the results broadly matching Trek’s interpretation that mineralisation deepens towards the south-east.

Mixed Regional Results

Outside Kuro, Trek completed drilling at the Nicks, Willis, Austin, Price, and Coogan prospects, with the final batch covering 70 holes across the project.

The Nicks, Willis, and Austin programs did not return significant copper or gold mineralisation, while narrow rare earth and niobium results at Price were isolated and adjacent samples were low.

Three holes tested an induced polarisation anomaly at Coogan intersected disseminated sulphides that may account for the geophysical response, however, the assayed intervals did not yield significant copper or gold mineralisation, prompting Trek to abandon a fourth planned hole.

“While the overall volume of mineralisation we have delineated at Kuro so far is limited, we have discovered what could be an entirely new district with the potential to host multiple centres of mineralisation across a vast distance,” chief executive Derek Marshall said.

“Our expanded tenure package encompasses geology that is highly prospective and virtually untested for high-grade manganese, and we see huge potential to build on this discovery.”

Targeting Wider Potential

Trek is combining drilling results with airborne surveys, ground geophysics, surface geochemistry, and geological mapping to rank prospects for the 2027 field season.

Its exploration effort will extend beyond the areas already drilled at Kuro as the group assesses whether other centres of mineralisation may be present across its wider Christmas Creek holdings.

Further target selection and drilling will determine whether Trek can extend the discovery and establish sufficient geological continuity for a future resource assessment.

“The reasons that Trek entered the region have been validated, with a new discovery coming out of this under-explored part of Western Australia,” Mr Marshall added.

“Trek remains well-funded, with an excellent working relationship with the local stakeholders, and a large landholding with excellent geological potential still to be explored.”

data.title: Anthropic's Australian data centre overwhelmingly opposed by residents
data.description:
A data centre planned in regional Australia with Anthropic as its anchor tenant is overwhelmingly opposed by residents, a filing for the project showed, setting the scene for a showdown between the AI company and the community hosting its first Australian facility.

Of nearly 600 public submissions on the proposed Western Downs Digital Park, about 250 km (155 miles) west of Brisbane, two expressed support for the project and one was neutral, according to the filing. The remaining 595 opposed it or asked for a delay until developers cleared certain environmental hurdles, the filing said.

"A significant number of submissions raise reasonable matters regarding water, power, noise, roads, housing and the scale of the project," the filing, lodged on behalf of developer Zerra DC, said.

Representatives of Zerra and Anthropic were not immediately available for comment.

The initial response, though far from binding, gives a sense of the souring relationship between communities and the so-called AI factories being built at pace around the world in a boom McKinsey has valued at $7 trillion by 2030.

Already in Australia, Goodman Group scrapped a roughly A$1.2 billion data centre planned for Sydney in September after a public backlash, while NextDC delayed a project in Melbourne amid resident concerns about energy use, triggering a shares selldown.

The Anthropic project is on farmland and further from the suburbs, but with a planned computing load of 1.44 gigawatts would be one of the country's biggest. About one-third of the submissions were from people who lived within 200 km of the site, the filing said.

Objectors mostly cited concerns about water use, electricity demand and prices, noise, road damage from construction traffic and pressure on housing.

Before the data centre project named Anthropic as its tenant on September 15, it had received five objections in a month, a log of public comments showed, with the rest arriving between then and November 11, when the local government stopped accepting submissions.

The filing about Australian data centre submissions was published the same week Anthropic made its stock market debut on Wall St, pricing its initial public offering on November 18 in a deal that valued the company at around $1.5 trillion.

data.title: BOJ Likely to Raise Rate in December or January Amid Persistent Inflation — Market Talk
data.description: The Bank of Japan is likely to raise its policy rate in December or January due to the combination of persistent underlying inflation, yen weakness and a more hawkish Fed, State Street Investment Management's Masahiko Loo says in a note. Both consumer inflation excluding fresh food and consumer inflation excluding fresh food and energy, were 2.2% on year, above the BOJ's 2% target. Combined with ongoing wage growth and a weak yen, the broader inflation backdrop remains consistent with continued policy normalization, Loo says. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)

data.title: Altimetrik Partners With Paysafe to Modernize and Scale Payments Technology
data.description:
Five-year agreement spans platform and product engineering, data and AI, and AI-led agentic operations

BENGALURU, India, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Altimetrik, an AI engineering company, has entered a five-year partnership with Paysafe (), a global payments platform built for the experience economy, to modernize and scale the technology behind its payments business.

Altimetrik will work across Paysafe's platforms and product engineering, data and AI, and AI-led agentic operations, using a product-engineering approach that ties delivery directly to business results. The engagement will support modernization and scaling, help strengthen the underlying data and machine learning foundation, and put AI to work across engineering and day-to-day operations to enable greater automation and efficiency.

"We know what it takes to keep a payments platform running around the clock and answerable to regulators because our teams have built and modernized these systems for banks and fintech leaders around the world," said Gautam Samanta, Chief Revenue Officer at Altimetrik. "We are proud that Paysafe has trusted us with its next phase of growth. Over the next five years, we'll bring AI into the core of its platform, so it keeps getting faster and more dependable for the customers who rely on it."

"We wanted a specialist partner that works with our product teams and answers for business results, and Altimetrik brings that, along with the AI capability to help us move faster," said Bob Legters, Chief Product Officer at Paysafe. "With this partnership, our engineers can focus on the product roadmap and the customers it serves. We look forward to working together with Altimetrik to make an even better payments platform."

Altimetrik will bring agentic delivery, in which AI agents take on parts of the engineering work, and AI-led operations into Paysafe's live payments systems, with human oversight, auditability, and accuracy built in from the start.

"Our commitment is to grow with Paysafe over the years, expanding our teams as the program moves deeper into engineering, data, and operations," said Vikram Chandna, Business Unit Head, Banking and Financial Services at Altimetrik. "Over time, we'll have several hundred engineers across the U.S., Latin America, and India working as part of each product team, helping new products reach customers faster."

The partnership will also include improving system reliability during peak payment periods, Salesforce engineering, and user experience engineering.

Learn more about how Altimetrik leads the future in banking and finance with secure, personalized solutions.

About Paysafe

Paysafe is a global payments platform built for the experience economy. We connect businesses, consumers, and fans across gaming, iGaming, video gaming, esports, events, travel, hospitality, online trading and digital commerce, helping lift every day and high-engagement experiences through reliable payment solutions. These include card payments, digital wallets such as Skrill, PaysafeWallet, eCash products like PaysafeCard, and a broad set of local payment methods. With approximately 2,800 employees across 12 countries and $167 billion in annualized volume in 2025, Paysafe focuses on making digital experiences easier to access and pay for.

Altimetrik is an AI engineering company helping some of the most revered and iconic enterprises modernize systems, data, and processes at the heart of their business, so they can move faster, operate more efficiently, and innovate continuously. Through ALTi AIOS™, its AI-native operating system, Altimetrik combines the latest AI capabilities with deep engineering expertise to help clients solve complex challenges, accelerate modernization, and deliver measurable outcomes at scale.

Altimetrik's clients get access to the latest AI innovations while maintaining flexibility to choose the right technologies for their business, through trusted relationships with OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic, Databricks, and major hyperscalers.

A member of the World Economic Forum's Centre for AI Excellence, the Forum's global hub for shaping responsible AI, Altimetrik is also recognized in the 2025 Constellation Research ShortList™ for Global AI Services and named a Major Contender in multiple Everest Group PEAK Matrix® assessments, including Software Product Engineering Services (2026), Enterprise Quality Engineering Services (2025), and Digital Engineering Services for BFSI and Life Sciences. data.title: Japan says JT dividend cut will not disrupt government's industrial investment plans
data.description:
By Makiko Yamazaki

Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday that the government's industrial investment programme would not be affected by Japan Tobacco's decision to cut its dividend following the loss of control of its Russian business.

The government owns a 37.55% stake in Japan Tobacco and uses dividend income from the cigarette maker as a source of funding for industrial investment.

"Even after the revision to the dividend forecast, there is no possibility that industrial investment will be hindered," Katayama told a regular news conference.

Japan Tobacco said on Thursday it will record a loss and lowered its annual dividend forecast by 25% after losing control of its Russian subsidiaries when President Vladimir Putin ordered their seizure this month.

The Russian units, which had accounted for around 25% of group profits, will no longer be included in its consolidated earnings, the company said.

Shares of Japan Tobacco slumped more than 8% early on Friday.

The Japanese government booked 156 billion yen ($977.02 million) in income from its JT holdings into its special account for the year ended in March.

($1 = 159.6700 yen)

data.title: Tips Films announces proposed voluntary delisting - What 8,000 retail shareholders need to know
data.description:
Tips Films Ltd. has announced a voluntary delisting offer in an exchange filing on Thursday, November 19. The company intends to buy out the rest of the public shareholders stake and take the company private.

The announcement was issued on behalf of the acquirers by Inga Ventures Pvt. Ltd., acting as the Manager to the Offer under SEBI delisting rules.

The proposal comes from two promoters of the company, Kumar S Taurani and Ramesh S Taurani, who plan to acquire the remaining shares held by public shareholders. Once completed, the shares would no longer trade publicly on either BSE or NSE.

What Does The Delisting Proposal Include?

The delisting proposal covers 10,81,770 fully paid-up equity shares of Tips Films Ltd., each with a face value of ₹10. This block represents 25.02% of the company's paid-up equity share capital held by public shareholders.

Promoters, at the end of the September quarter, had a 74.98% stake in the company, of which, promoters Kumar and Ramesh Taurani own 40.5% stake, with the rest by promoter group members and entities.

Why Are Promoters Proposing The Delisting?

The acquirers outlined three main reasons for pursuing a full buyout and taking the company private:

One, full ownership by the acquirers along with other promoter group members is intended to give the company more operational, financial, and strategic room to maneuver—including supporting business operations, carrying out corporate restructurings or acquisitions, exploring new financing structures with promoter group support, and investing in the company.

Two, going private is expected to reduce ongoing compliance expenses and free up management time currently spent on continued stock exchange listing requirements so leaders can focus more on the business.

Lastly, the offer gives public shareholders a chance to get immediate liquidity and a certain value for their shares amid elevated market volatility, priced according to SEBI delisting regulations.

Conditions For Delisting To Go Through

The delisting price will follow rules for determining a "Floor Price" and calculating the price under those regulations, with the floor price and fixed delisting price to be announced separately in due course.

The delisting proposal is not final yet and depends on several required steps and approvals:

Due Diligence and Board Approval: A Peer Reviewed Company Secretary must complete required due diligence, and the company's board of directors must approve the delisting proposal.

Shareholder Vote: Shareholders must pass a special resolution approving the proposal, with votes from public shareholders in favor at least twice the number of public shareholder votes against it.

Regulatory and Exchange Approvals: Approvals from the stock exchanges and any required statutory, regulatory, or third-party consents must be obtained.

Share Tender Threshold and Offer Documents: Enough equity shares must be validly tendered for the delisting to succeed under SEBI rules, subject to any additional terms set out in the upcoming Detailed Public Announcement, Letter of Offer, or related updates.

Shares of Tips Films saw a sharp spike towards the close of the session on Thursday, ending 7.2% lower on Friday at ₹392. The stock is still down 8% so far for the year.

data.title: Sri Lanka central bank surprises with key rate hike on inflation fears
data.description:
Sri Lanka's central bank raised its key policy rate by 25 basis points in a surprise move on Friday, citing higher-than-expected inflation pressures caused by volatile global energy prices.

Markets had expected the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) to stay put for a third consecutive meeting after a surprise hike of 100 basis points in May.

Sri Lanka, which imports all its fuel, has increased prices by about 35% this year, resulting in inflation shooting up from 2.2% in March to 8.3% last month.

The CBSL said in a statement that while global energy prices have eased recently, the impact of previous increases is expected to exert pressures on prices in the near term.

"Latest projections also showed that inflation could remain higher in the near term and for longer than previously projected, before returning to the target of 5% in the second half of 2027," the statement said.

"Inflation expectations, particularly in the one-year period ahead, have also risen recently, although medium-term inflation expectations remain anchored around the target," it said.

data.title: Japan Inflation Accelerates on Surging Cost of Daily Necessities — Market Talk
data.description: Higher oil prices amid Middle East tensions are increasingly feeding into Japan's consumer prices, particularly for daily necessities and durable goods, says NLI Research Institute economist Taro Saito. Inflation for daily essentials such as tissue paper, plastic bags and facial cleansers accelerated for a sixth straight month in October, rising 6.9% from a year earlier, from April's 1.5% gain, according to NLI estimates. "Higher crude oil prices are being passed on to retail prices with a time lag through rising costs for petrochemical products and packaging materials," Saito says. "Inflation for durable consumer goods is also steadily accelerating, driven by rising semiconductor and memory prices amid expanding global AI-related demand," he adds. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)

data.title: GME Stock Rises Overnight: Roaring Kitty’s Return After Nearly 2 Years Flips Retail Sentiment Bullish Amid GTA 6 Frenzy
data.description:
Key points:
  • Keith Gill, known as Roaring Kitty, returned to social media and posted a Cat Mario image. 
  • GameStop is also drawing attention following the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI and Trump’s share buy.
  • On Stocktwits, retail sentiment turned ‘bullish’ from ‘bearish’. 

GameStop Corp. (GME) stock edged higher overnight after Keith Gill, better known as Roaring Kitty, returned to X with his first post since January 2025. His mysterious Cat Mario image appeared alongside the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, sparking fresh interest among bullish retail traders who hoped for a repeat of the 2021 “meme stock” squeeze.

GameStop stock edged up 0.4% overnight Thursday after a 1.5% gain in regular session. The stock is also on track for a third week of gains.

Roaring Kitty Breaks Nearly Two-Year Social Media Silence

On Thursday, Gill dropped a single image of Cat Mario, the power-up from Nintendo’s Super Mario 3D World, on an account that had been silent for nearly two years. He added no caption or explanation.

Gill is the reason GameStop became the “meme stock”. His bullish commentary in 2020 and 2021 helped fuel a retail rally that squeezed hedge funds and turned him into a folk hero on Reddit. Since then, his posts have usually sent the stock higher.

GTA VI Launch, Trump Purchase Adds To GameStop Buzz

Roaring Kitty’s return to social media comes after the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which is expected to bring more shoppers to GameStop stores to buy consoles and accessories. However, GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen is speaking out against the industry's growing shift toward digital game sales. He believes this change is bad for customers and could hurt GameStop's traditional business of selling physical video games.

Also, a U.S. government disclosure revealed that President Donald Trump bought between $1,001 and $15,000 worth of GameStop's stock.

What Are GME Retail Traders Saying

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock jumped to ‘bullish’ from ‘bearish’. The stock registered a 210% increase in message volume over the past week.

A user said, “Got silver and gold crashing while gme trending over kitty post !”

Another user said, “This is a totally different company to what it was 5/6 years ago. Cash in the bank. Invested in other ventures. Profitable, with really good margins. Management that is heavily invested. And it goes on and on.

Seems like RK is back on the scene , but even if he’s not, this investment is going to be fantastic. Can’t wait to see what develops in the future.”

A third user said, “Any chance this is a big nothing burger? Trying to stay optimistic but the chances of 2021 happening are slim to none.”

GME stock has gained 34% year-to-date.

data.title: How High Can ANT Stock Go? Wall Street Debut Sparks Valuation Debate – One Analyst Sees Amazon-Google Scale Opportunity In Anthropic
data.description:
Key points:
  • Needham put Anthropic in the same league as Amazon, Google and Microsoft.
  • Melius set the highest target at $155 over two years, nearly 60% above the debut close.
  • NYU Stern’s Aswath Damodaran valued Anthropic at about $76, citing higher data center costs and regulatory pressure.

Shares of Anthropic PBC (ANT) jumped 17% in their Wall Street debut on Thursday as analysts cast the Claude maker as a rare growth opportunity in the same league as Amazon and Google, with the most bullish target pointing to nearly 60% more upside.

ANT stock opened at $111.50 on Thursday before settling at $97.17, well above its $83 offer price even on a day the Nasdaq Composite fell over 2%.

The $81.34 billion offering overtook SpaceX’s June listing as the largest IPO on record. Alongside a separate $26 billion private placement, Anthropic expected to receive $104.8 billion after fees and expenses, giving it cash to fund the next generation of Claude.

Analyst Puts Anthropic In Big Tech’s League

Needham initiated coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating and a $150 target, implying 54% upside from current levels. “Growth opportunities like ANT rarely come along but we think history puts ANT in the same dominant bucket as fellow tech titans AMZN, GOOG, and MSFT,” the firm said.

Needham estimates that AI could address a tenth of the $56 trillion global labor market. Anthropic already earns more when customers put Claude to work on more tasks. Usage-based charges accounted for 79% of revenue in the first nine months of 2026, according to its prospectus.

Needham expects revenue to grow more than 150% in fiscal 2027 and believes Claude’s brand and Anthropic’s scale could drive operating margins above 35% over time, even as the company spends tens of billions of dollars a year training models.

William Blair also expects Anthropic to win a larger share of corporate budgets. “We think AI is a generational shift in the tech landscape, and Anthropic is leading the charge in developing AI with a select handful of other companies,” the firm said.

William Blair initiated coverage at ‘Outperform,’ calling the IPO valuation “very reasonable” at nine times estimated 2027 sales. It said a multiple of 17 to 20 times sales could put the stock at $130 to $150, or 34% to 54% above its debut close.

What It Would Take ANT To Hit $155

Melius initiated coverage at ‘Buy’ with a two-year target of $155, implying nearly 60% upside from Anthropic’s $97.17 debut close. The firm expects customers to use Claude more often and buy more products as the cost per task falls. Over time, it sees earnings power above $5 a share and operating margins above 30%.

Melius also pointed to Anthropic’s flexibility. Claude can run on chips from Nvidia and AMD, as well as Amazon’s Trainium and Google’s TPUs. “If the model scales accordingly, shares could trade at a nice premium to hyperscalers given its outsized growth and high gross margins,” the firm said.

Additionally, Wolfe Research initiated coverage at ‘Outperform’ with a $135 target, implying 39% upside from the same close.

Cathie Wood Sees Edge In Unreleased Models

Citizens pointed to Claude’s role in building its own successor as a reason for its ‘Market Outperform’ rating. “Over 90% of the contributions to our codebase in September 2026 were written by Claude,” Anthropic said in its prospectus. Citizens’ $125 target implies 28.6% upside from the debut close.

Meanwhile, ARK Investment Management CEO Cathie Wood sees an edge in the models Anthropic keeps in-house. She estimates AI training costs are falling about 75% a year, allowing Anthropic to train better models while giving rivals fewer chances to learn from its most advanced work. Wood compared the potential lead over open-weight models to a decade of progress at the slower pace of earlier chip advances. “It would be like being 10 years ahead in that world,” she said.

ANT Valuations Below Debut Close

Morningstar kept its fair value estimate at $92, about 5% below Thursday’s close, with a ‘3-star’ rating. It sees Claude’s meeting and spreadsheet tools as an early test of whether businesses will shift spending from existing software to Anthropic as Claude takes on more valuable work. With about $900 billion in computing commitments, Morningstar believes Anthropic’s cash and IPO proceeds can cover its near-term bills even if sales stop growing. A drop in sales would be tougher. “I think declines in revenue would be quite difficult for the company to manage,” Morningstar said.

Similarly, NYU Stern professor Aswath Damodaran valued Anthropic at about $76 a share after accounting for employee options, which is 22% below its debut close. His estimate assumes higher data center construction costs and tighter regulation will weigh on profits.

How Do Retail Traders Feel About ANT?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ANT was ‘extremely bullish’ amid a 885% surge in 24-hour message volumes.

One user said they would buy at $65. Another user said they would wait for $75. A separate user said they were sticking with Nvidia, Intel and SpaceX, adding, “Long-term holding has always been my strategy, and I’m not changing it now.”

View this Stocktwits post

Most voters in a Stocktwits poll sat out Anthropic’s debut, with 68% of the 17,500 votes going to “Avoiding it.” Another 16% chose to buy for the long term, 9% favored a short-term trade and 7% planned to trade around the volatility.

data.title: CelcomDigi 4Q Earnings Likely Higher on Quarter — Market Talk
data.description: CelcomDigi's 4Q core net profit could grow further sequentially, driven by additional cost savings and higher revenue, CIMB Securities analysts Choong Chen Foong and Kenny Lim say in a note. They tip 2026 core net profit to grow by 7% on year, driven by stronger revenue and Ebitda margin. Earnings could dip 1% in 2027 due to its share of Digital Nasional's losses, partly offset by revenue growth, merger synergies and lower integration costs, they reckon. CelcomDigi also plans to reduce Digital Nasional-related costs through greater infrastructure sharing, improved procurement and operating synergies, they note. CIMB cuts CelcomDigi's target price by 10% to 3.30 ringgit, while maintaining a buy rating. Shares are 2.8% lower at 2.41 ringgit. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
